card.text: Explore Titan in 3D with cssEarth. See through Saturn’s largest moon’s haze with Cassini near-infrared imagery.

introduction.text: Saturn’s largest moon hides beneath thick haze. Methane rain feeds its rivers and lakes, while dark dunes cover the equator.

normal.title: Controlled infrared mosaic
normal.summary: Surface features show through the haze, along with clouds and seams. Detail varies; the gray grid marks missing observations.

radar.title: RADAR global mosaic through T126
radar.summary: Brightness shows radar backscatter rather than elevation or visible color. The gray grid marks areas without measurements.

topography.title: GTDR measured heights
topography.summary: Adjusted Cassini altimetry and SARtopo measurements above the 2575.0 km reference sphere. The 2019 archive grid covers about 6.0% of Titan by area; gray grid preserves unmeasured cells. Source posting is 0.125° (about 5.62 km at the equator), with variable observation footprints. Height colors do not deform the sphere.

interpolated.title: GTDR interpolated topography
interpolated.summary: Interpolated model between adjusted Cassini altimetry and SARtopo tracks, above the 2575.0 km reference sphere. Broad patterns between tracks are model estimates. Original missing cells remain gray. Compare Measured height and Distance to data to judge observational support. Height colors do not deform the sphere.

coverage-distance.title: GTDR distance to measurements
coverage-distance.summary: Distance to the nearest input measurement in the GTDR topography solution, in kilometres. Large distances identify interpolation far from data. This is neither height uncertainty nor a measure of every Cassini instrument’s coverage. Original missing cells remain gray; tiny negative source roundoff is displayed at zero.

geology.title: Cassini global geomorphology · Lopes et al. (2020)
geology.summary: Explore Titan’s dunes, plains, highlands and lake basins in the global Cassini interpretation.
